questions.question: What does a language server add to an AI coding workflow?
options: A second GPU attached to the editor
Automatic approval of every pull request
Diagnostics, navigation, and completion
A replacement for the Python runtime
questions.explanation: A language server analyzes source as you edit and feeds diagnostics, symbol navigation, and completion to the editor. It does not execute the program or supply hardware.

questions.question: Which editor settings are part of the lesson's evaluate_editor checklist?
options: dark_mode, emoji_completion, and automatic model retraining
video_recording, browser_history, and cloud billing
only a wider minimap and a custom file icon
The five capabilities in REQUIRED_SETTINGS
questions.explanation: REQUIRED_SETTINGS names five workflow capabilities. evaluate_editor returns the satisfied and missing names plus a score without changing the settings.

questions.question: What is the practical effect of enabling format-on-save and basic type checking?
options: Formatting and static type warnings
Every runtime shape error is proven impossible
The editor compiles CUDA kernels on save
Notebook outputs are automatically converted into unit tests
questions.explanation: Formatting and static analysis catch common consistency and interface mistakes early. They complement, rather than replace, runtime tests for tensor shapes and device behavior.

questions.question: Why use Remote SSH when the GPU is in another machine?
options: It copies the remote GPU into the laptop's hardware inventory
It runs the editor context on the remote host
It removes the need for authentication on the remote host
It changes a CPU notebook into a CUDA kernel without moving execution
questions.explanation: Remote SSH installs the editor server on the GPU host and runs commands there. This keeps data and computation remote while providing a local editing interface.

questions.question: The editor shows no GPU, but an SSH terminal on the same project host runs nvidia-smi successfully. What should you check?
options: Whether the editor's font has GPU glyphs
Whether the project contains more Markdown than Python
Check the remote window and selected interpreter
Whether the laptop battery is fully charged
questions.explanation: The shell result proves the host can see the device, not that the editor is connected to that host or using its Python. Re-selecting the remote window and interpreter addresses the mismatch.

questions.question: You alternate between local notebook exploration and a remote training box. Which editor setup is the best fit?
options: Disable the integrated terminal and edit remote files through screenshots
Use a new editor for every notebook cell so no settings can be shared
Run training locally because editor settings determine available hardware
Use local notebook support and Remote SSH
questions.explanation: The checklist supports both interactive notebooks and a remote execution context. Recording the interpreter avoids accidentally running the training job with the laptop environment.
